sents.t: On Saturday morning, the line outside Sunrise Bakery started at six, even though it was snowing.
Lily had been up since three, baking.
“I’m so nervous,” she whispered.
“What if nobody likes my croissants?”
“Break a leg,” I said.
“It means good luck.”
“I know what it means,” she laughed.
“But I’m a baker, not an actress!”
At seven, she opened the doors.
The first customer was Rosa, of course, with Max.
Then came Mr. Brooks, Walter, Jasmine, Dr. Kim, and half of my podcast listeners.
Even the reporter from the Oakville Times came to take photos.
By ten o’clock, the croissants were selling like hotcakes.
“That’s another idiom,” Mr. Lee told me.
“It means they’re very popular.”
I was serving coffee behind the counter, and at first I felt like a fish out of water.
But after an hour, it was a piece of cake.
At noon, a little boy looked at a cupcake for a long time, but his mom said they only had money for bread.
Lily gave him the cupcake.
“It’s on the house,” she smiled.
By four, everything was sold out.
Lily sat down and finally relaxed.
“We did it,” she said.
“You did it,” I said.
“I just poured the coffee.”
